analysis: What changed versus the 4:00 AM brief: the split tape held but did not improve much — Nasdaq-100 futures are +1.50% (vs +1.47% at 4 AM), S&P futures faded to +0.17% (from +0.36%) and Dow futures worsened to -0.96% (from -0.72%). The VIX is compressing, 26.79 vs Thursday's 28.18 close, which the overnight crowd read as a bullish tell. The earnings story widened in both directions: Moderna beat big and raised guidance, AppLovin's +31% Thursday close (missed by the 4 AM brief) and Cloudflare's +20% premarket print show beats still get paid — but Atlassian fell 16% premarket despite beating EPS, so the print alone is not enough; guidance and narrative decide. The bounce's trigger is under fresh scrutiny: HN's most-discussed Anthropic thread argues the lab's growth flattened before the reported $80B ARR, a direct counterweight to the report that sparked the chip rebound. Bitcoin slid 4.6% to ~$75,900, a risk-off tell running against the equity bounce. Signal vs noise: the VIX compression, the breadth of the chip rebound (SOX names +4-10% premarket), and the earnings dispersion are signal; the premarket bounce on thin volume, the recirculated month-old Apple order-cut report, and the 'Friday pump, Monday dump' framing are noise until payrolls at 8:30 AM ET and the open confirm them.

community_signals.takeaway: A 228-point, 280-comment HN thread (Nov 2-3) arguing Anthropic's growth flattened, with S-1 figures showing $33.2B revenue against $18.8B compute costs in the first three quarters of 2026 — the counter-narrative to the reported $80B ARR that triggered last night's chip bounce. The debate centers on whether labs can reach profitability at current valuations or whether cheaper models commoditize the lead.
community_signals.title: Anthropic's growth just flattened

headlines.headline: The split tape held into 5 AM PT: as of 7:55 a.m. ET, Nasdaq-100 futures were +1.50% at 27,154, S&P 500 futures +0.17% at 7,395, Dow futures -0.96% at 51,118 and Russell 2000 futures +0.18%. The VIX fell to 26.79 from Thursday's 28.18 close.
headlines.why_it_matters: The Nasdaq-led bounce is intact but narrow — the Dow still falling and the S&P barely green says the rotation out of tech is not done, and the VIX compressing is the one cleanly bullish tell.

headlines.headline: Moderna reported Q3 2026 results before the open: revenue $1.313B, up 29% year over year and well above the ~$885M consensus, EPS of $0.38 vs an expected $1.25 loss, net income of $162M vs a $200M loss a year ago. It raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 15-25% from up to 10% and lifted year-end cash guidance to $8.1-8.3B. Shares bounced premarket after falling 7% on Thursday.
headlines.why_it_matters: A genuine beat-and-raise driven by overseas COVID vaccine sales — the kind of report that normally leads the tape, but it is one name against a broad chip-led rout.

headlines.headline: AppLovin closed Thursday +31.04% at $356.10 after Q3 revenue of $2.18B (+55.5%) and Q4 revenue guidance of $2.38B, above the $2.25B estimate; net income was $1.44B, up 72%, on volume 4.0x its average. It is -1.43% premarket Friday, giving back a little of the move.
headlines.why_it_matters: The biggest single-name earnings win of the week — a beat-and-raise that ran 31% on a day the tech sector averaged -5.49%, proving the selloff is about AI infrastructure funding, not earnings broadly.

headlines.headline: Cloudflare extended its after-hours gain into premarket, +20.21% to $294.95 — the top gainer among the 500 largest US stocks. Airbnb followed at +14.35%. Both reported Thursday after the close: Cloudflare Q3 revenue +39% to $782.5M with raised full-year guidance; Airbnb Q3 revenue +19% to $4.87B with a $12B buyback.
headlines.why_it_matters: Software earnings are being paid in full while chips bounce on short-covering — the market is rewarding proven revenue growth and punishing unproven buildout spending.

headlines.headline: Atlassian fell 15.98% premarket to $154.00 — the biggest loser among the 500 largest US stocks — even though non-GAAP EPS of $1.65 beat the $1.43 consensus.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat that still gets sold 16% is the mirror image of Cloudflare — the print alone is not enough; guidance and the growth narrative decide the move.

headlines.headline: Apple is the only Magnificent Seven name lower premarket, -1.21% to ~$340, while Nvidia is up ~4% and Amazon +0.43%; Microsoft -0.89% and Meta -0.15%. A premarket-movers post circulating this morning cites the iPhone 18 Pro component-order-cut report — but that report is from Nikkei Asia on Oct 9, a month old, and was already priced in.
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple is lagging the bounce on no fresh company news — the order-cut story being recirculated is stale, so the softness reads as relative weakness rather than a new demand signal.

headlines.headline: December Fed hike odds are now about 65-70%, down from 83% before Thursday's selloff, per Reuters and Kitco. Bloomberg Economics expects payrolls to rise just 26,000 — well below the +59,000-65,000 consensus — with unemployment near 4.2%, a print it says would not deter the Fed from a December hike.
headlines.why_it_matters: The market has repriced the hike down but not out — payrolls at 8:30 a.m. ET decide whether the Fed or the market gives way first.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. The $0.525 per-unit distribution pays TODAY, Friday Nov 6, to holders of record Oct 26. The Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. On the call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.

watch_next: 8:30 a.m. ET today: October nonfarm payrolls (consensus +59,000-65,000 jobs, unemployment expected to hold at 4.2%; Bloomberg Economics expects just +26,000); Michigan consumer sentiment at 10:00 a.m. ET. USAC's $0.525 distribution pays today.
Whether the premarket chip bounce holds into the open or fades like Thursday's morning bounce did — QQQ 658 is the line WSB is watching; a break below Thursday's lows reopens the correction leg.
Any confirmation or denial of Musk's SoftBank turbine-default claim, and Anthropic IPO timing/valuation news — both are funding-chain questions for the AI buildout.

Earnings today: Vistra's Q3 call at 3:00 p.m. ET (full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance $6.8-7.6B, excluding the Cogentrix deal and Meta contract); Oklo and TeraWulf report today after falling 13-14% on Thursday.
Fed speakers through the day; December hike odds now about 65-70%, down from 83% before Thursday's selloff.
